Arbiter self-dogfood: uses findInlineSuppression() from lib.mjs for INV-12 inline suppression support. Target template does not have this dependency yet.

Arbiter self-dogfood: inlines getRepoRoot() and readTaskState() instead of importing from lib.mjs, making it self-contained for the arbiter repo's own task-lifecycle enforcement. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-29, #1092.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: imports suppressions-shared.mjs and exports findInlineSuppression for inline-suppression directive support (INV-31). These arbiter-internal imports must not be back-ported to the template shipped to target projects.

Arbiter self-dogfood: hardcodes 'npx prettier --check .' (validate, not auto-fix, to avoid silent file changes) and 'npx eslint src __tests__' as the scopeCommandToFile inputs, whereas the template feeds the formatCommand/lintCommand config variables. Both scope to the single edited file via scopeCommandToFile (#1515); the divergence is only the hardcoded vs config-driven command source. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-29, #1092; updated #1515.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: contains CI Linux runner note specific to arbiter repo: 'CI Linux jobs run on self-hosted runner docker-ci-build via repo variable CI_BUILD_RUNNER_LABEL'. This is arbiter-specific infrastructure context, not appropriate for target project templates. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-29, #1092.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: includes check-no-direct-spawn.mjs (arbiter-internal hook with no .ejs template yet) and check-no-any.mjs (generated from languageHook body not .ejs template), and a different UserPromptSubmit structure with matcher:* group. These were added directly to arbiter's .claude/settings.json without being back-ported to the template. (Materialization tracked in #1090; whole-file exemption to be narrowed there.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: CANON-16 Survey gate (#458) is implemented in both arbiter's materialized hook and the EJS template; the logic is identical. Cosmetic divergence only: Prettier formats the materialized hook with double quotes and the EJS template with single quotes. Functionally equivalent.

Arbiter self-dogfood: hooks.mjs dispatcher (#248) not yet materialized in arbiter's own .claude/hooks/ — arbiter's settings.json continues to use individual hook wiring (see existing settings.json divergence). Materialization deferred to a dedicated regenerate pass after all Wave-1 issues land.

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook uses dynamic await import() of scripts/detect-track.mjs (RT-EH-001 — static ESM import of a missing shared lib crashes all commits). Generated target hooks have equivalent regexes baked in at arbiter init time via EJS include; dynamic import is an arbiter-self-config-only pattern not shipped to target projects. Additionally, the self-config FE block emits 2 lines (vitest + tsc) while ts/frontend.ejs emits 3 (adding pnpm snapshot diff reminder) — intentional: arbiter's self-config is more conservative than generated target advice.

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook carries one extra FAIL-OPEN-INTENT documentation comment clarifying the exit-code contract (0 for non-PR commands, 2 on explicit gate-fail). Comment-only divergence, no behavioural difference. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-30, #1118; restores the #1090 raw-hook allowlist entry that was dropped from the merged commit.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook adds repo-root scoping and inline-suppression support via findInlineSuppression() from lib.mjs (INV-21 directive). The shipped template omits the lib.mjs dependency, so the suppression branch cannot be back-ported without shipping arbiter-internal lib.mjs changes. Divergence is by design. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-30, #1118; restores the #1090 raw-hook allowlist entry dropped from the merged commit.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook scopes enforcement to the repo root and drops AGENTS.md from READ_ONLY_PATTERNS because arbiter AUTHORS its own AGENTS.md (it is the source), whereas a target project's AGENTS.md is generated and must stay read-only. Back-porting the repo-root bypass was empirically proven to break the INV-36 HARD-hook contract. Divergence is by design. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-30, #1118; restores the #1090 raw-hook allowlist entry dropped from the merged commit.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook scopes the unused-export check to the single edited file for fast per-edit execution in arbiter's own repo; the shipped template runs the broader project-wide check. Divergence is by design. (Confirmed intentional 2026-05-30, #1118; restores the #1090 raw-hook allowlist entry dropped from the merged commit.)

Arbiter self-dogfood: the arbiter-self wiki-on-commit.mjs is a direct copy of the template (no EJS expressions). Divergence is zero but the dogfood check compares against the rendered template output which may differ in whitespace. Divergence intentional (#1241, 2026-06-06).

Arbiter self-dogfood: materialized hook protects docs/internal/METHOD/, docs/internal/SYSTEM/DECISIONS, docs/internal/SYSTEM/CANON.md, and docs/internal/ADR/ — arbiter's own self-governance docs moved under docs/internal/ (T7, #1770, docs/public-internal split). The shipped template still protects the generic docs/METHOD/, docs/SYSTEM/DECISIONS, docs/SYSTEM/CANON.md, docs/ADR/ paths, since target projects generated by arbiter do not adopt this internal/ split. Divergence is by design (2026-07-04, #1770).

A3 (wave1 action plan, FP-6a): the dast-full (OWASP ZAP full scan) job is removed entirely from self. Arbiter is a CLI with no running service and no docker-compose.yml — the job could never have a real target, so it was permanent dead weight (`if: false`, un-runnable) rather than a genuinely-disabled-with-a-plan gate. The template still emits this job for downstream projects: `if: false` for non-service archetypes (discoverable/re-enablable, CANON-18-tested) and ACTIVE for service archetypes with a real target. That template behavior is intentional and unchanged — this divergence covers only self's stricter removal.

The template collapses 01-pr-fast.yml.ejs's entire PR pipeline (gate, unit tests, security-early-fail, dependency-review, iac-scan, docs-check, sonar-scan, debt-gates, ci-required, post-merge-gate — contract/integration/behavioral tests moved to 02-pr-extended.yml.ejs at #1875) to a one-line solo-dev-gate stub whenever `locals.enableSoloDevMode` is true — and arbiter.json sets features.soloDevMode: true. Self deliberately keeps running the full peer-review-shaped pipeline regardless (arbiter dogfoods harder than its own declared collaborationMode: trunk-solo — same pattern documented in check-ci-tiers.mjs.ejs's cadence-parity comment). Tracked under #1900.

Self runs `node scripts/build-kit.mjs` before `npm run test:e2e:bake` (the bake fixtures need arbiter's own kit catalog); the generic template's e2e:bake step does not need a kit build (kit is an arbiter-self concept, not something a generated target project has). Tracked under #1900.

Self is the typescript/library archetype's own release: it runs npm-package-publishing guards (check-pack-size.mjs, check-tarball-contents.mjs, `zip -r release-artifact.zip`) that only apply to the @arbiter/cli tarball, absent from the generic multi-archetype template render for this profile. Large diff (many other-archetype release steps this profile doesn't hit) — NOT individually audited line-by-line; R-01/R-09 (census) already track 05-release template↔self parity as a dedicated follow-up. Tracked under #1900.

Self sets `enableNativeBakeE2E` (bake-e2e-native + generated-gate-e2e [per-language matrix] + generated-gate-e2e-misc jobs) — a flag with no wiring path in resolveProjectConfig/src/generators (grep confirms zero setters): a manual arbiter-self-only harness augmentation for the init→bake native-fixture-smoke matrix + VITEST_L2 generated-gate harness (split per-stack, B5 gate-thesis reliability). The template comment says as much: "Downstream-generated projects do not ship this harness, so it renders only for arbiter itself." Tracked under #1900.
